q: 1. The best method of procurement for complex and work of specific nature is
explain: Complex, specialised works need wide competition and expertise, so International Competitive Bidding (ICB) is used.

q: 2. Pre-tender stage requires
options: finalization of designs and preparation of estimate
explain: The pre-tender stage specifically requires finalizing designs and preparing detailed estimates before the tender is floated.

q: 3. While bid evaluation, if unit rate and total amount are contradicted, then which of the following will prevail
options: unit price is adopted and total amount is corrected
explain: The unit price governs, and the total amount is corrected by arithmetic.

q: 4. Bid bond is ……… % of quoted amount.
explain: Per the answer key, 2.5%.

q: 5. The formula for determination of price adjustment in a work contract may not contain
explain: Price adjustment formulas typically use contract price, adjustment amount, and material/labour price indices, but do not directly include equipment cost as a variable.

q: 6. Bidding document is prepared
explain: Bidding documents must be finalized and prepared before the tender notice is published so bidders can obtain and use them.

q: 7. Mobilization advance upto 20 % of the cost of work is given to a contractor
options: on commencement of work at site for payment of loan taken by him
for the purchase of construction material
for the payment of advances to labour and other staff
for all activities required to start the work at site on finalization of contract document
explain: Mobilization advance is granted to help the contractor cover all initial startup activities (equipment, materials, staff) needed to begin work at site after contract finalization.

q: 8. Pre-Qualification document should be approved by
explain: D would have been the beast answer but AS PER BOOK A .Depending on the level and type of public entity, pre-qualification documents can be approved by the Director General, chief of public entity, or a class-I gazetted office chief - any of the above.

q: 9. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: A schedule of rates lists item descriptions and their current unit rates without specifying quantities, unlike a tender document or estimate.

q: 10. The pre-tender stage of construction requires
explain: All of these are done before tendering.

q: 11. The pre-tender stage of construction requires:
explain: The pre-tender stage involves site selection, land acquisition, and design finalization - all necessary before floating the tender.

q: 12. The post tender stage of construction consists of
explain: All of these happen after tendering.

q: 13. According to "Contract Act 2055" the number of classes of contractor are
explain: The Nepal Contract Act/Public Procurement regulations categorize contractors into four classes: A, B, C, and D.

q: 14. Within the relationship among client, engineer and contractor, no agreement is required between
explain: The engineer typically acts as the client's representative under the main contract; no separate formal agreement exists directly between the engineer and the contractor.

q: 15. Whle filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers quotation?.
explain: Site conditions, labor pricing, and technical specs are critical inputs when pricing a bid[cite: 1].

q: 16. Tender is called for i) to minimize the cost of an item ii) to find exact rate of item of unknown item iii) to take minimum rate from contractor
explain: Tendering promotes competition to ensure the owner receives the most economical price (minimum rate) for the work.

q: 17. Local tender is not favorable due to following reasons:
options: most of the material used locally
engineer or site in charge pressurized
explain: Local tenders can sometimes lead to localized pressure or influence on the decision-making staff compared to international competitive bidding.

q: 18. Quality and cost based selection (QCBS) method is used
options: Progress of work up to a stage
explain: QCBS is a standard method used to select consultants by evaluating both technical quality and cost of their proposals.

q: 19. A turn key contract is offered for
explain: A turnkey contract involves the contractor handling every stage from design to completion so the owner can 'turn the key' and start using the facility.

q: 20. Amicable settlement means
explain: Amicable settlement is a non-adversarial process where the parties resolve the dispute themselves through negotiation.

q: 21. A contractor can start the construction works following the receipts of
explain: The 'Notice to Proceed' is the formal authorization that marks the official start date of the project.

q: 22. While making the agreement of any contract, the legal authority is appointed by
explain: A single entity (the owner/client) typically establishes the legal framework for the contract document.

q: 23. What are the essential components of a valid contract?
explain: An enforceable contract mandates mutual offer/acceptance, free consent, legal capacity, and consideration[cite: 1].

q: 24. The post tender stage of construction consists of
explain: The post-tender stage includes work assessment, expenditure tracking during execution, and final account settlement - all these activities.

q: 25. For the construction of a project, a contractor is a
explain: A contractor can be a legally registered individual, a partnership firm, or a corporate agency.

q: 26. The maximum amount for approval of tender by Gazetted 3^{rd} class officer is (Source:PPR 2064(67))
explain: Rule 67 limits Gazetted 3rd class officers' tender approval power to under NRs 3 crore (30 million)[cite: 1].

q: 27. At present, in Nepal the types of contract normally followed in housing project to save the government taxes is
explain: In small-scale housing, owners often provide materials themselves and contract only for labor to reduce tax liability.

q: 28. *The amount of money deposited while bidding a tender as a guarantee of the party's willingness of carry out the work is called
explain: Earnest money (bid security) ensures the bidder is serious and will sign the contract if awarded.

q: 29. The first step for formulation of any contract is
explain: Contract formulation begins with inviting bids from the public or pre-qualified vendors through publishing the tender notice.

q: 30. The amount of money deposited while bidding a tender as a guarantee of the party's willingness of carry out the work is called
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or bid security is deposited along with the bid submission to prove the bidder's genuine intent to undertake the work.

q: 31. A muster roll is:
options: attendance sheet of temporary workers for remuneration
inventory list of equipment and list of people on the site
list of jobs the workers must do on site
several drawing sheets of site rolled in a bundle
explain: A muster roll is the attendance record of temporary/casual workers used to calculate their wages/remuneration.

q: 32. As per Public Procurement Act/Regulation minimum time required for tender notice is :
explain: For national competitive bidding in Nepal, the standard notice period is 45 days.

q: 33. Contract completion report is a summary of
options: Financial summary of payments including variation orders and claims
explain: A contract completion report summarizes contract description, financial payment details, and the taking-over certificate - all of the above.

q: 34. The minimum number of consulting firms for direct purchase of service is
explain: Per the answer key, 3.

q: 35. Residential buildings are treated as
explain: In terms of construction scale and structural loading, residential housing is generally classified as light construction.

q: 36. The document announcing to prospective bidders that the owner is ready to receive the bids is called:
explain: An Invitation for Bids (IFB) or Notice to Bidders publicly notifies qualified contractors that an employer is accepting bids for a project.

q: 37. The supplementary specification prepared and applied if the standard specification does not cover the requirement of works under a contract is called:
explain: When general or standard specifications fall short for unique requirements, performance or special technical specifications are appended.

q: 38. Which of the following is not Bid document?
explain: The Letter of Acceptance (LOA) is issued after evaluation during award stage; it is not a part of the original issued bidding documents.

q: 39. An offer in writing to execute some specified civil works at certain rates within a fixed time under certain conditions of contract is called :
explain: A bid (or tender) is the formal written offer submitted by a contractor in response to an invitation to work.

q: 40. Which of the followings should be practiced first if a dispute arises in a contract?
explain: Amicable settlement (direct negotiation between parties) is typically the first step attempted before escalating to mediation, adjudication, or arbitration.

q: 41. Force majeure in contract is:
options: occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure covers unforeseeable extraordinary events beyond reasonable control (such as natural disasters or war) that prevent contract fulfillment.

q: 42. Percentage of retention money is equal to ……… % of each payment made to the contractor.
explain: Per the answer key, 5%.

q: 43. In a sealed quotation, the successful bidder should deliver the performance security within ……… days of receipt of letter of acceptance.
explain: Per the answer key, 7 days.

q: 44. A surety bond issued by an insurance company or a bank that provides legal guarantee to the owner or employer that the bidder will sign the contract if it is awarded to him is called
explain: Bid security is the surety bond guaranteeing that the successful bidder will sign the contract if awarded.

q: 45. The money deposited by the contractor as the guarantee of tender is known as
explain: Bid bond and earnest money are both tender guarantees.
